findings.title: PID reuse merges unrelated process provenance while source loss stays green
evidence: Process identity is only PROC:<pid> and existing nodes retain old label/edges.
Malformed rows and source failures are skipped while run reports health 100.
findings.impact: Forensic ancestry and blast radius can join unrelated process lifetimes and look complete.
mitigations: No current production consumer was found
findings.recommendation: Key by PID plus birth/ProcessGuid and boot identity; retain source-event links, rejected counts and cursor completeness; degrade health for any gap.

findings.title: Purple Guard policy loss silently disables reviewed drills at health 100
evidence: Missing, malformed or wrong-type policy becomes an empty dict.
An empty policy performs no detection and is reported as health 100 learning mode.
findings.impact: Installed assurance drills can disappear without a fail-visible control state.
mitigations: Protected data root normally limits writers
findings.recommendation: Authenticate/version the policy, retain expected-policy state, distinguish unconfigured from lost/tampered, and show path plus parse/authentication error below health 100.

findings.title: Ransomware detection ignores every nested user directory
evidence: Entropy candidates and rename snapshots use one top-level os.scandir per watched root.
Subdirectories and permission/read skips have no coverage counter while existing roots yield health 100.
findings.impact: Encryption confined to ordinary nested Documents/Pictures trees bypasses both ransomware signals.
mitigations: Other sensors may observe file changes
findings.recommendation: Use bounded recursive no-reparse traversal or journal telemetry with durable cursors and depth/file/time budgets; expose visited/skipped/truncated counts and never claim 100 without fresh subtree coverage.

findings.title: Disable-driver remediation accepts any Windows service name without driver identity
evidence: _svc accepts arbitrary driver text or the stem of any .sys path.
matches never proves service type, image, signer, vulnerable digest or BYOVD policy before sc config disables it.
findings.impact: An admitted weakness can disable an unrelated critical service or boot/system driver.
findings.recommendation: Require a typed authenticated BYOVD record bound to service object, kernel-driver type, stable image, pinned signer/hash policy and freshness; deny critical services and bind operator approval to the exact target.

findings.title: Free-text weakness fields can authorize process termination or broad firewall blocks
evidence: Network isolation extracts the first IP from generic fields/display text and admits private, multicast and reserved peers.
Kill matching grants irreversible authority when generic display text contains a trigger substring.
findings.impact: Poisoned/misleading posture evidence can kill a benign exact process or block essential network infrastructure.
mitigations: Kill path requires live PID/create-time/image identity
findings.recommendation: Remove display-text matching and require authenticated typed response contracts with action, exact target, authority, corroboration, expiry, nonce and plan-bound approval.

findings.title: Remediation rolls back stale service/registry state without external-state compare-and-swap
evidence: Prior service/registry state is captured before durable preparation.
Apply does not re-prove the retained prior value and rollback unconditionally restores that snapshot.
findings.impact: GPO, MDM, administrator or security-product changes during dispatch can be overwritten and later undone.
findings.recommendation: Retain object identity and observed version/value, apply with compare-and-swap, refuse conflicts, and compensate only when current state equals Angerona's committed postcondition.

findings.title: Remote Bridge sessions have no forward secrecy
evidence: Mutual proofs and AES-GCM session keys derive only from one long-term PSK and public nonces.
No ephemeral DH or credential epoch/rotation protocol exists.
findings.impact: Recorded telemetry can be decrypted after later PSK compromise.
findings.recommendation: Use TLS 1.3 mTLS or a reviewed ephemeral authenticated handshake, rotate node credentials, bind role/node/protocol identities and expose credential/cipher age.

findings.title: Governor can suppress security sensors and leave stale throttles after restart
evidence: Criticality is inferred from mutable display names/category, leaving many sensors throttleable up to 8x.
No finally reset exists; a new level-1 governor never applies 1x when low load leaves stale sibling throttles.
findings.impact: Detection windows can widen under induced pressure and stay widened after governor restart while health is 100.
findings.recommendation: Use immutable criticality metadata and manager-owned expiring throttle leases, reset/reconcile on lifecycle boundaries, enforce minimum deadlines and degrade health for incomplete application or telemetry.

findings.title: Self-Healer permanently consumes crash snapshots before successful diagnosis
evidence: Snapshots are marked seen before parse/source/model/stage success and pre-launch snapshots are ignored.
A following empty poll overwrites model/poll failure health with 100.
findings.impact: Transient failure permanently loses a real crash diagnosis while the module looks complete.
findings.recommendation: Use durable NEW/PROCESSING/RETRY/STAGED/REJECTED states with bounded retry/dead-letter, authenticate and size-bound snapshots, constrain source root and score health from pending age/outcomes.

findings.title: Self-Integrity trusts current runtime and silently omits missing enforcement targets
evidence: arm fingerprints whatever code is live, skips unresolved targets and reports 100 even with zero targets.
Fingerprints omit mutable global/helper dependencies; ACL collection failures/weaknesses do not lower health.
findings.impact: Pre-arm tamper, missing imports or helper replacement can become trusted baseline behind a green enforcement claim.
mitigations: Runtime replacement of a watched callable is detected
findings.recommendation: Verify a signed release manifest, require every mandatory target and dependency closure, fail closed on unresolved/ACL collector errors and expose expected/watched counts plus exact source lines.

findings.title: Shadow-copy dedup and coverage are PID-only and fail green
evidence: Dedup is keyed only by PID despite collecting create_time.
Command/access failures become empty nonmatches without counters, then health 100.
findings.impact: Rapid PID reuse or inaccessible process metadata can hide a recovery-tamper command.
mitigations: Exact trusted-tool argv required for host response
findings.recommendation: Key by PID/create-time/executable, ingest short-lived process-create telemetry, expose readable/denied/failed totals and lower health for incomplete coverage.

findings.title: SIEM health 100 means socket handoff, not collector ingestion
evidence: sendall/sendto success immediately deletes the durable row.
No application receipt exists, yet an empty queue reports health 100.
findings.impact: A collector/proxy can accept and discard evidence irrecoverably behind a green module.
findings.recommendation: Support idempotent RELP/HTTPS application ACK, retain until authenticated ACK and separate transport-handoff health from end-to-end delivery sequence/age.

findings.title: Honeytoken tamper handling enables memory exhaustion and repeated critical alerts
evidence: The attacker-controlled decoy path is read to EOF without type/size bound.
Restaging refuses the existing tampered file, so it retriggers every 2.5 seconds; creation is check-then-open.
findings.impact: In opt-in user-folder mode the detected actor can OOM the EDR or flood its event store.
mitigations: Default deployment is under protected runtime data
findings.recommendation: Use no-follow stable identity, exclusive create, bounded anchor-length reads, safe quarantine/rename before restage, incident/object dedup and live/failed/tripped health.

findings.title: Both SOAR loops commit revision cursors before processing the batch
evidence: Priority/general cursors are assigned current before returned events are processed.
Only legacy timestamp delivery advances after each event.
findings.impact: One exception/generation failure can suppress later serious events in the same retained batch on same-instance restart.
findings.recommendation: Commit per-event only after a terminal receipt, persist idempotent delivery IDs, retry/dead-letter failures without advancing siblings and expose lag/drop/error age.

findings.title: Active SOAR can report old receipts as a new mitigation
evidence: Receipt matching uses timestamp/module rather than a unique request ID.
When no new receipt appears, applied falls back to all prior matches and mitigated becomes true.
findings.impact: A failed/asynchronous duplicate event can be shown as contained by an old action.
mitigations: Combat owns actual mutation and signed action receipts
findings.recommendation: Issue a fresh correlation/action-request ID bound to evidence and target digests, require a new receipt for it and report timeout as pending/unmitigated without fallback.

findings.title: Speculative Triage reports 100 despite no production consumer, stale frames or model failure
evidence: Repository search found get_primed only at its definition.
Frames are PID-only with no expiry; queue/full and model failures do not affect loop health 100.
findings.impact: Advertised latency benefit is absent and a future consumer can reuse an unrelated stale process prompt.
findings.recommendation: Wire a typed consumer or mark unavailable; bind frame to birth/image/incident, enforce TTL/single-use, count drops/model failures and score successful reusable frames.

findings.title: Privileged storage migration reopens mutable pathnames after safety scan
evidence: Legacy source derives from mutable LOCALAPPDATA.
Tree/reparse checks precede string-path shutil move/delete; per-item check still leaves a cross-volume swap window.
Unreadable/unsafe source can become find_stray false and health 100.
findings.impact: An unprivileged spill-tree writer can race opt-in elevated migration into copying/moving a different or reparse-backed tree into protected runtime data.
findings.recommendation: Use OS canonical profile, fixed-root directory handles, no-follow stable identities and handle-relative exclusive moves; run unelevated where possible and report unsafe/inaccessible as degraded.

findings.title: Module discovery executes an unpinned top-level syscall_bridge import
evidence: Import-time import syscall_bridge uses ambient sys.path without fixed package/digest/signer/ACL/reparse/ABI checks.
A substitute can execute during discovery and return plausible SSNs for health 100.
Fallback HANDLE calls lack explicit ctypes prototypes.
findings.impact: A writable import/current directory can become arbitrary code execution under the suite token, especially in portable/elevated launches.
mitigations: Protected installed/frozen layouts reduce writable search paths
findings.recommendation: Package in a fixed private namespace, seal to release manifest publisher/digest/ACL/no-reparse, isolate native code behind a least-privileged authenticated broker, validate ABI/protocol and declare native prototypes.

findings.title: Sysmon cursor cannot prove log generation continuity and persistence failure is green
evidence: Authenticated cursor stores only channel and record number, so a cleared/refilled range can contain the old number and skip the new prefix.
Missing HMAC authority only sets last_error during save; tail drain/open can still look healthy.
Reopen after read error does not reseek durable cursor.
findings.impact: Clear/wrap/restart can lose or duplicate retained security events without an accurate health state.
findings.recommendation: Bind cursor to channel generation/file identity and event anchors, fail health on persistence loss, reseek every reopen, emit exact loss ranges and show cursor age/sequence plus rejection counts.

findings.title: Temporal correlator health never follows its live assessment state
evidence: Health is set once at startup to 35 or 70.
Stable, missing, blind, overflow and recovered assessments emit events but never update score/note.
findings.impact: The row can overstate blind coverage or remain unnecessarily degraded after recovery.
mitigations: Assessment events explicitly label coverage state
findings.recommendation: Derive atomic health from each assessment state, persistence, drops and evidence age; recover only after a complete window and link current continuity reason/state file.

findings.title: One failed USB identity probe can transfer trust to replacement media
evidence: Swap detection requires both old/current identities nonempty and different.
One empty current identity overwrites known identity; a later different known identity no longer triggers swap, while trusted mount record remains.
findings.impact: Replacement media can inherit Angerona workflow trust after a transient identity failure.
mitigations: Module does not claim OS device denial
findings.recommendation: Revoke trust when a trusted identity becomes unknown, preserve last-known identity, bind approval to device instance plus insertion epoch, revalidate before every scan and expose identity coverage health.

findings.title: Watchdog does not detect the hung modules advertised by its contract
evidence: Dead detection checks only error status or a dead thread.
A live blocked running thread has no cycle heartbeat/deadline test.
Restart counters never decay and terminal-down alerts repeat each sweep.
findings.impact: A required sensor can hang indefinitely while watchdog says all healthy; repeated failures can exhaust budget and storm alerts.
findings.recommendation: Use manager-owned generation/cycle heartbeat deadlines, restart leases/backoff, stability-based budget decay, deduplicated terminal alerts and health tied to required sibling freshness.

findings.title: WFP Controller neither uses WFP telemetry nor proves network coverage
evidence: WFP initialization only loads fwpuclnt; refresh always uses IP Helper tables.
Map is only protocol/local-port and overwrites address/family collisions without remote endpoint/state.
Missing APIs, table errors, psutil absence or empty results still allow health 100.
findings.impact: Advertised WFP/outbound detection can be blind or misleading and repeatedly false-alert on local endpoints.
mitigations: IPv4 and IPv6 IP Helper enumeration
Containment API itself is dry-run/approval/broker gated
findings.recommendation: Implement versioned WFP/ETW net-event telemetry or rename capability; retain full tuple/direction/PID birth/image/sequence, count source errors/collisions, deduplicate and cap health by proven coverage.

findings.title: Disconnect/reconnect is a deterministic Evil-Twin detection bypass
evidence: Disconnect/query failure sets last state to None.
Next connection is informational and immediately enrolled even when known SSID has new BSSID.
Failed initial probe parks permanently; later failures do not lower health; baseline is volatile TOFU.
findings.impact: A nearby attacker can force disconnect then lure reconnect to a new Evil Twin without the advertised alert.
mitigations: Other TLS/NDR controls may detect downstream behavior
findings.recommendation: Differentiate error/disconnect, retry startup, persist authenticated operator-approved SSID/BSSID/security baselines, evaluate reconnect before enrollment, use native WLAN events and expose freshness/coverage.

findings.title: A 10000-file prefix can starve YARA coverage indefinitely
evidence: Traversal stops after 10000 files per root without continuation/rotation/truncation state.
Every cycle restarts at filesystem order; enumeration and per-file scan errors do not lower health 100.
findings.impact: An attacker can populate Downloads so a malicious file stays outside the repeatedly scanned prefix.
findings.recommendation: Use a durable fair cursor/rotation by stable identity, prioritize new/changed files, publish visited/skipped/truncated/timeout and oldest-unscanned age, and lower health for incomplete roots.

reviews.evidence: PID-only process lifetime and green source gaps.
Lost policy becomes health-100 learning mode.
Strict bounded manifest, observe-only output and degraded invalid/missing health held.
Only direct child files observed.
Threshold authorization, payload verification and authenticated floor held; local pathname root limit is already documented.
reviews.recommendation: Prefer opened-object verification in updater integration.

reviews.evidence: Target authority and external-state conflict defects.
reviews.recommendation: Typed authenticated targets plus resource CAS.

reviews.evidence: PSK-only session derivation.
Brittle exemptions and stale throttle lifecycle.
At-most-once snapshot handling.
TOFU baseline and optional targets.
Scoped digest-bound restore exists; known legacy trigger_rollback remains with no production caller.
reviews.recommendation: Remove/private-gate legacy sink and object-bind caching.

reviews.evidence: PID-only suppression and incomplete collection health.
Socket handoff is terminal delivery.
Unbounded attacker-controlled read and restaging storm.
Precommitted cursor; known R5-03 PID-only corroboration remains separate.
Precommitted cursor and stale receipt attribution.
Unused/stale frames and green failures.
Authenticated baseline/broker, bounded object reads, explicit source coverage/retry and observe-only output held.
reviews.recommendation: Retain hostile-config and channel continuity regressions.

reviews.evidence: Safety-check/use race on privileged migration.
Ambient import executes unpinned native/Python artifact.
Generationless cursor and green persistence loss.
Health frozen at startup assessment.
Unknown identity can carry trust across replacement.
No hung/stale detection.
Advertised WFP/outbound telemetry is absent.
Reconnect bypass and volatile TOFU.
Deterministic scan-cap starvation.
reviews.recommendation: Fair durable traversal and coverage health.
